sections.h2: Phase III is about fifteen times the size of the intra-state phase before it

chart.title: The third phase dwarfs both earlier schemes in approved money
chart.source: Cabinet releases (PIB); Ministry of Power for GEC-I.

sections.means: The Cabinet approved the largest transmission scheme yet backed for renewable energy, with the first intra-state phase to pay for batteries.
sections.todo: Track progress against the roughly 7,300 circuit kilometres a year the scheme needs from 2026-27 to 2032-33.

sections.h2: Only 26 GW of the 44 GW meant for the two earlier phases is connected

chart.title: Only 26 GW of the 44 GW meant for the two earlier phases is connected
chart.sub: Renewable capacity under the two earlier phases, GW, by March 2026.
chart.source: Figures as cited in the post.

sections.means: Two earlier phases were meant to connect 44 GW, and by March 2026 only 26 GW had been connected.
sections.todo: Measure each new phase by connected gigawatts, not by money approved.

sections.h2: The Centre pays 29% overall, and storage gets less central support than lines

chart.title: Storage gets 12% central support, against 33% for lines
chart.sub: Central support as a share of each component's outlay, %.
chart.source: Cabinet release; component split as reported by trade press.

sections.means: The grant covers a third of the lines but only 12% of storage, and what is left is recovered through transmission charges in tariffs.
sections.todo: Publish the full component split from the scheme guidelines so the reported figures can be checked.

sections.h2: Central support per MWh of storage has fallen from ₹28 lakh to ₹12 lakh

chart.title: Central support per MWh of storage has fallen with each round
chart.sub: Central support per MWh of battery storage, ₹ lakh.
chart.source: Cabinet releases; per-MWh figures are this blog's division.

sections.means: Support per MWh has fallen with each round, as battery prices have, which leaves less subsidy for each megawatt-hour of storage.
sections.todo: Set out how each battery's discharge duration and cost split between transmission charges and generators will be decided.
